task: Add explicit signed platform tenant-context resolution for privileged platform actors without changing presentation surfaces.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Canonical tenant resolution for privileged platform actors is high-risk because a wrong context can cross customer boundaries. The context must be explicit, signed, actor-bound, current-authority validated and fail closed.

acceptanceCriteria: A short-lived signed tenant-context token binds actor UUID, instance UUID and expiry.
Canonical instance resolution honors the token only for the same authenticated actor with a current platform_operators role.
A valid explicit target is resolved by exact instance id and only for pilot/active status.
If the explicit target is unavailable or current platform authority is missing, resolution returns null instead of another tenant.
Configured deployment tenant and pilot acceptance precedence remain unchanged.
Normal merchant role_binding resolution remains unchanged when no valid actor-bound platform context exists.
invariants: DOMAIN-TENANCY remains the single tenant-selection authority.
The cookie cannot grant platform authority and is revalidated against server-owned platform_operators.
No first-tenant, first-membership or ambiguous multi-tenant fallback is introduced.
The admin tenant-context signing domain and cookie are distinct from storefront pilot acceptance.
A different authenticated actor cannot consume another actor's token.

failureModes: A browser-controlled tenant id becomes authoritative without cryptographic proof.
A signed instance-only token leaks across users on the same browser.
A revoked platform actor retains cross-tenant access until token expiry.
A stale explicit target silently falls through to a different membership candidate.
The normal platform token accidentally broadens storefront pilot acceptance.
edgeCases: Platform actor with zero store memberships can still resolve one explicitly selected tenant.
Platform actor with multiple bindings resolves only the signed target.
Expired or tampered token contributes no explicit context.
Merchant actor without a matching platform row cannot consume the token.
Configured deployment slug still resolves before the platform context.

alternatives.summary: Store only the selected instance id in an HttpOnly cookie.
alternatives.reason: HttpOnly limits script access but does not authenticate the tenant value and cannot prevent tampering or cross-user reuse.

alternatives.summary: Persist a selected tenant pointer on the platform user record.
alternatives.reason: A durable account-level pointer creates hidden cross-device state and can silently affect later sessions beyond the explicit browser workflow.

alternatives.summary: Use a short-lived HMAC token bound to actor, instance and expiry, then revalidate current platform authority during canonical resolution.
alternatives.reason: It provides explicit bounded context while preserving server authority and exact-target fail-closed semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: The resolver must remain in DOMAIN-TENANCY and not be implemented as a presentation-local selector.
specialistReviews.resolution: The token primitive and consumption both live under src/lib/instances, which is the canonical tenant context path.

specialistReviews.finding: Signing only the instance id would still let a later authenticated user inherit an earlier platform user's selected scope.
specialistReviews.resolution: The payload binds actorId and instanceId and the cookie reader requires an exact actor match before returning the selected instance.

specialistReviews.finding: Explicit selection must never degrade into another candidate when the requested target is stale or unavailable.
specialistReviews.resolution: A present valid selection performs one exact eligible-instance lookup and returns normalize(selectedData), including null, without entering role-binding candidate resolution.

challenge.scenario: Actor A's token remains after Actor B authenticates.
challenge.finding: Cross-user tenant leakage would be possible without actor binding.
challenge.resolution: Token payload and reader require the current actor id to match exactly.

challenge.scenario: Token signature or expiry is modified client-side.
challenge.finding: Tampered context must not influence tenant truth.
challenge.resolution: HMAC verification uses a domain-separated key and timingSafeEqual; invalid or expired input returns null.

challenge.scenario: Platform role is revoked while a valid token remains.
challenge.finding: Token possession must not preserve cross-tenant privilege.
challenge.resolution: Current platform_operators authority is queried on each selected-context resolution and absence/error fails closed.

challenge.scenario: Selected tenant is archived or suspended.
challenge.finding: Resolver could otherwise pick another membership candidate.
challenge.resolution: Exact selected lookup is limited to pilot/active and returns null directly when no eligible row exists.

challenge.scenario: A deployment has WEBSHOP_INSTANCE_SLUG and also receives a platform token.
challenge.finding: Browser context must not override deployment-bound tenant scope.
challenge.resolution: Configured-slug resolution remains earlier in the canonical resolver.

challenge.scenario: Preview pilot acceptance and platform tenant context coexist.
challenge.finding: Normal context must not become storefront acceptance authority.
challenge.resolution: Pilot acceptance remains separate, with a different cookie/signing domain and existing precedence.

proofPlan: Add deterministic regression proof for actor-bound signing, tamper/expiry rejection markers, exact target resolution and no-fallback ordering.
Run Incremental Known Failure Replay for the isolated auth/access subsystem.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure.

requirements.requirement: Canonical instance resolution supports a short-lived actor-bound signed platform tenant selection, revalidates current platform authority, and resolves only the exact eligible target without fallback.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A token selected by one actor cannot resolve for a different authenticated actor.
An unavailable explicit selected target cannot fall through to another tenant.
Pilot storefront acceptance remains distinct from platform tenant context.

notes: Second isolated transaction in the MR1 platform tenant-selection block. Base is the scope-classification branch so release-risk diff contains only the high-risk tenant/auth authority. Sentinel semantic review corrected the Completion Contract scope strength from 3 to 2 because the strongest referenced evidence producer (GUARD-QUALITY-TESTS) proves scopeStrength 2; retaining 3 would be an overclaim.
